clue.text: Wave after couple's decisive match

indicators.note: the wave comes after the couple, so its word follows in the answer

parts.note: to couple is to tie or join together; the 's reads as 'has' and links
a breaker is a large wave crashing on the shore

explanation.surface: A wave of momentum follows a pair's victory in a deciding match.
explanation.definitionFit: When scores are level, an extra game or set settles the contest, and that deciding game is this.

clue.text: Picture India game being thrown

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the letters of game are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A snapshot of India losing a match, the game being thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a visual representation, which is the ordinary sense of this word.

clue.text: Let's rob abandoned pad

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters of let's rob run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to burgle a flat that has been left empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' looks like slang for a home, the thing being robbed, but here it means a cushion or padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolster is a long stuffed pillow or cushion, a kind of pad.

clue.text: Author Blyton? Not one to finish

indicators.note: not one means the word for one is left out of the author's first name

parts.note: Enid Blyton was the prolific English children's author of the Famous Five books
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question about whether Enid Blyton would be the one to complete a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to bring it to a close, a straightforward synonym of complete or finish.

clue.text: Learning rising political policy maker on left has advantage

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a wonk is a policy expert, especially in politics
an edge is an advantage, as in having the edge over rivals

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming policy adviser on the political left has an advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning in the sense of acquired information and understanding is a synonym of this word.

clue.text: Restore Magritte perhaps beginning to wear

parts.note: René Magritte was the Belgian surrealist painter

indicators.note: beginning to wear means the first letter of that word is taken

explanation.surface: A Magritte painting starting to show wear needs restoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to make it fresh again, which is what restoring does.

clue.text: Like a piano given by singers including heartless tenor

indicators.note: the singers' word takes the trimmed tenor inside it

parts.note: a song given by singers has been sung

indicators.note: a heartless tenor loses its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A piano accompanies some singers, though their tenor lacks feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano has strings stretched across its frame, so it is a stringed instrument.

clue.text: Everything inside we had closed off

indicators.note: the word for everything goes inside the contraction

parts.note: we had contracts to we'd, written without the apostrophe
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything we kept indoors was shut away.
explanation.definitionFit: A walled area is enclosed by walls, so it is closed off from the outside.

clue.text: Decorated old Royal Navy mate losing millions

indicators.note: losing means the letter for millions is taken out of mate

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A decorated veteran of the Royal Navy has lost his old shipmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornate is highly ornamented, elaborately adorned with decoration.

clue.text: Intensity of feeling is hard to take in

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
to take in food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Strong emotion can be difficult to absorb.
explanation.definitionFit: In the heat of the moment means at a peak of passion, so heat is strong emotion.

clue.text: Illegal tunnel regularly very poor

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of tunnel is taken

parts.note: awful means very bad or very poor in quality

explanation.surface: A shoddy tunnel built outside the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlawful breaks the law, the plain sense of illegal.

clue.text: Purely oral nutrient, strangely including whiskey

indicators.note: the rearranged nutrient takes the letter for whiskey inside it
strangely means the letters of nutrient are put into an odd new order

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A nutrient taken by mouth, oddly with whiskey in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwritten rules or traditions are passed on by word of mouth only, never set down on paper.

clue.text: Fine new missile

parts.note: an arrow is a missile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A precise new weapon described as fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine in the sense of thin or slender, as in a fine line, matches this adjective.

clue.text: Admitted Authorised Version had debts to others

parts.note: AV is the abbreviation for the Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible
someone who had debts owed money

explanation.surface: A confession that a Bible edition was published while in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowed belief is one openly declared or confessed, so it has been acknowledged.

clue.text: Physical ruin of reservoir wall with time

parts.note: a dam is the wall holding back the water of a reservoir
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A reservoir's wall crumbling over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm done to an object, spoiling it physically, is what this noun describes.

clue.text: Maazel's stardom regularly revealed a great conductor

indicators.note: regularly means alternate letters of Maazel's stardom are taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Lorin Maazel's fame showed him to be a fine conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorin Maazel was a celebrated American conductor, so the surface sits in the answer's own world.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, the title given especially to an eminent conductor.

clue.text: On the verge of critical attack ousting the British

indicators.note: ousting means the letter for British is pushed out

parts.note: a broadside is a fierce verbal attack, originally a volley from all the guns on one side of a ship
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Someone poised to launch a fierce critique that drives the British out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the verge of' reads as 'about to', but verge alone is the definition: the grass strip beside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A verge is the grassy edge beside a road, the strip at the roadside.

clue.text: Profundity of department head's introduction

indicators.note: the introduction of head is its first letter

explanation.surface: A deep opening speech from the head of a department.
explanation.definitionFit: Profundity means deepness, of water or of thought, which is the meaning of this noun.

clue.text: Relaxation from brainteasers

indicators.note: from means the answer is taken out of the run of letters in brainteasers

explanation.surface: Puzzles as a way to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of rest and comfort, free of strain, like relaxation.

clue.text: Caught a whiff of fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of smell, used in British English
second meaning: a small silvery fish of the salmon family

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests noticing the smell of fish; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Smelt is the British past tense of smell, and also the name of a small edible fish.

clue.text: Cruel tyrant kills editor on return

indicators.note: on return means the combined word for kills and editor is read backwards

parts.note: to top someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A brutal dictator has a newspaper editor murdered when he comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power oppressively, an autocrat.

clue.text: Note the right tie

parts.note: TE is a variant of ti, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale; the answer also runs through 'Note the right' by coincidence, with no hiding signal

explanation.surface: A reminder to put on the correct necktie.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope that ties an animal to a post, and to tether is to tie up.

clue.text: What's towards end of shoe?

parts.note: to means towards, as in walking to the shops

indicators.note: end of shoe means the last letter of that word

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which part lies at the far end of a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The toe is the front tip of a shoe, the part covering the digits of the foot.

clue.text: From now on fetch heron for cooking

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of fetch heron are mixed up and made into something new

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring a heron to be cooked from today onward.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforth means from this time forward, a formal way of saying from now on.
